papers.title_en: TamedFlow: Trajectory-Aware Distillation for Teacher-Assisted Diffusion Sampling
papers.authors: Shuaiqi Cheng, Jiahao Zhang, Boyuan Gu, Yuxi Chen, Haiying Xu, Zexin Lu, Huiyu Zhou, Xuming Hu
papers.evidence: 通过轨迹感知蒸馏加速扩散采样
papers.tldr: DiT 高保真生成但推理需大量串行评估，压缩与自适应推理结合时会出现“Combination Gap”。TamedFlow 用跨架构特征对齐、近恒等速度对齐头与随机 rollout 监督训练压缩学生模型，并在推理时用轻量 LTE 路由草稿。将 DiT-XL/2 蒸馏到 DiT-B/2 后，在 ImageNet 256×256 上达到 FID 2.58 和 2.25× 实测加速。该工作揭示并缓解部署态轨迹失配，为教师辅助扩散采样提供新方案。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) deliver high-fidelity image and video generation, but inference requires many sequential model evaluations. Two acceleration strategies are increasingly important: model compression makes each evaluation cheaper, while adaptive inference avoids selected teacher computation through reuse, forecasting, or speculative execution. Their combination, however, is brittle: directly applying the evaluated adaptive methods to a compressed student can degrade quality, an observed failure mode we call the \textbf{Combination Gap}. We link this gap to a mismatch between pointwise distillation and short-horizon execution: a student trained at teacher states need not remain reliable when its own predictions are chained. We propose \textbf{TamedFlow}, which trains a compressed DiT for this deployed role through cross-architecture feature alignment, a near-identity Velocity Alignment Head, and randomized rollout supervision. At inference, a lightweight Learnable Trajectory Estimator routes completed drafts: accepted drafts bypass the teacher, while rejected drafts roll back and receive one teacher rescue step. Distilling DiT-XL/2 into DiT-B/2, TamedFlow reaches FID $2.58$ at $2.25\times$ measured speedup over DDIM-50 on ImageNet $256\times256$. Ablations support trajectory supervision, and routing controls favor LTE over random decisions at nearly matched latency. Evaluations on ImageNet $512\times512$, MS-COCO, and Latte/FaceForensics extend the empirical scope.

papers.authors: Frank-Peter Schilling, Daniel Barco, Philipp Denzel, Marc Stadelmann
papers.evidence: 用于三维图像合成的扩散模型
papers.tldr: 医学影像本质为三维体数据，扩散模型在图像保真度和样本多样性上表现突出，但三维建模带来显存、算力与训练数据的高需求。本文系统比较面向医学图像的3D扩散模型，覆盖CT、MRI、PET等模态及数据增强、域迁移、重建、修复和伪影校正等任务。文章还梳理以患者特征、报告、分割掩膜或其他图像为条件的生成方式，并分析当前性能与局限。最后给出未来研究方向，为医学三维生成建模提供参考。
papers.abstract_en: Generative deep learning methods such as Variational Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks or Diffusion Models have achieved remarkable results in image synthesis. In particular, Diffusion Models have demonstrated superior image fidelity and sample diversity compared to other approaches on standard benchmarks, while also offering more flexible training dynamics as evidenced both in natural image domains and in medical applications. In medical imaging including Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Positron Emission Tomography, such models have various important use-cases including data augmentation, domain transfer, image reconstruction, inpainting, image augmentation and artifact correction. Further, generated images can be conditioned on patient characteristics, medical reports, segmentation masks or other images. Specific challenges arise due to the 3D volumetric nature of medical images, which translate to substantial demands in terms of memory, compute, and training data. This article provides a comparative overview of 3D Diffusion Models which have been developed for medical images, with a focus on current performance, limitations, and an outlook for future work.

papers.title_en: DiffLTM: Continuous Diffusions Large Tabular Models for Conditional Generation
papers.authors: Alankrita Bhatt, Mukur Gupta, Andrea Montanari, Pulkit Tandon
papers.evidence: 用于条件表格数据生成的连续扩散模型
papers.tldr: 面向大型表格模型的条件生成需同时处理数值与类别混合、类别高基数且分布失衡，以及稀有子群生成困难等问题。DiffLTM 采用连续扩散框架，并对类别变量使用交叉熵损失，首次给出理论依据，同时扩展条件生成以支持新型条件形式。作者还提出聚焦稀有子群的评价指标，实验显示模型生成质量强，且基于劳动力数据训练后能复现计量经济学经典洞见。
papers.abstract_en: Conditional generation is a key capability to be supported by Large Tabular Models, enabling a number of applications. Accurate conditional generation has to contend with two key challenges: $(i)$ Data comprise a mixture of numerical and categorical entries, the latter often with high cardinality and heavily unbalanced proportions; $(ii)$ Conditional generation becomes increasingly difficult for rare sub-populations. The best models in this class use a hybrid of continuous and discrete diffusions. In this paper, we design a continuous diffusion model with strong generation quality. An important element is the use of cross-entropy loss for categoricals, for which we provide a first theoretical justification. We introduce metrics that focus on rare subpopulations. Further, we generalize conditional generation techniques to enable new types of conditioning. Finally, we show that our model (trained on labor data) can capture classical insights from econometrics.   Code is available at https://github.com/granica-ai/DiffLTM

papers.title_en: Robot Motion Transition with Human Motion Prior
papers.authors: Taehyun Byun, Taemoon Jeong, Yoonbyung Chai, Woojin Wie, Insu Park, Kyungjae Lee, Sungjoon Choi
papers.evidence: 利用生成式人体运动先验连接人形运动片段
papers.tldr: 将独立获取的人形机器人动作连成连续长序列时，简单插值忽略边界位姿的相对位置、朝向与时长，生成式先验也可能因边界不佳产生多余移动或转向。STAMP 采用机器人到人再到机器人的流程，用学习到的对齐模型在人体动作空间中为后续动作排序候选位置、朝向和过渡时长，再由人体动作先验生成过渡。生成序列重定向回机器人并训练动作跟踪策略，在 Unitree G1 与 ROBOTIS K1 上验证了过渡跟踪成功，实机展示了长时程动作连接能力。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid motion-tracking policies can reproduce diverse behaviors, yet connecting independently acquired motions into a continuous sequence remains challenging. Interpolation connects boundary poses without considering whether their relative position, heading, and timing provide suitable conditions for a transition. A generative motion prior can produce richer motion, but poorly arranged boundaries may cause it to generate excessive locomotion, turning, or another unintended action. We present Spatio-Temporal Alignment with a Motion Prior (STAMP), a framework for connecting independently acquired humanoid motions through a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process. STAMP uses human motion space to draw on rich motion priors and reuse transition knowledge across robot embodiments. Its key component is a learned alignment model that determines the boundary conditions for motion inbetweening. Given the two motions retargeted to a human rig, the alignment model ranks candidate positions, headings, and transition durations for the following motion. A human motion prior generates the transition under the selected alignment. The completed sequence is retargeted to the robot and used as a reference to train a motion-tracking policy. We evaluate the tracking success of the generated transitions on Unitree~G1 and~ROBOTIS K1. Physical robot demonstrations further show that STAMP connects independently acquired motions into long-horizon sequences. Project page: https://childtoy.github.io/STAMP-project

papers.title_en: WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Chenxi Song, Yanming Yang, Tong Zhao, Ruibo Li, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Chi Zhang
papers.evidence: 视频扩散模型的相机轨迹对齐
papers.tldr: 视频扩散模型具备丰富3D/4D先验，但相机控制不精确、时空不一致且相机运动与场景动态耦合。WorldForge V2先以基于扭曲参考的无训练引导沿目标轨迹迭代生成，并用光流定位运动相关潜通道、双路径校正参考误差；v-cache降低细化开销。进一步把运动定位扩展到网络块，提出Trajectory LoRA并用两阶段训练适配引导生成状态。多数据集上实现SOTA生成质量与轨迹精度，且单场景训练可泛化到未见场景。
papers.abstract_en: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering. However, their use in spatial tasks is limited by imprecise camera control, spatial and temporal inconsistencies, and entangled camera motion with scene dynamics. Existing approaches, such as task-specific fine-tuning and post-process warping, often introduce visual artifacts, generalize poorly, or incur high computational costs. We propose WorldForge V2 to achieve accurate camera control while preserving the generative capabilities of pretrained video models. We first develop a training-free guidance framework using warped references to iteratively refine generation along a target camera path. Optical-flow analysis identifies motion-related latent channels for selective guidance, helping separate motion control from appearance. A dual-path strategy further compares guided and unguided predictions to correct artifacts from imperfect references. Together, these components guide viewpoint changes while preserving scene appearance and object motion. To reduce refinement costs, v-cache approximates the correction using the preceding denoising prediction, avoiding an additional model evaluation. We further extend motion localization from latent channels to network blocks and introduce Trajectory LoRA, which concentrates adaptation on blocks most responsive to trajectory guidance. A two-stage training strategy teaches these adapters to denoise the states encountered during guided generation, using limited supervision effectively. This enables reliable camera control with very little training data, with a single training scene already supporting generalization to unseen scenes. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations across multiple datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and trajectory accuracy in camera-controlled video generation.
